Draw the boundaries first. Where the layers divide is the one decision that gets expensive once code sits on top of it. Everything else can be rewritten in an afternoon. So this is the part that gets the time. Keep the core free of the framework. Business logic that imports nothing can be tested without a browser, a server or a database. Push the side effects out to the edges. What is left in the middle stays simple enough to reason about. Secure before there is data. Row-level security is switched on before the table has a single row, and every policy denies by default. A permission you never granted is not one that can leak. Write it down. Every project I own has its architecture and conventions written down. Somebody new, or a language model, can read it cold and do useful work inside an hour." src="./assets/page/how-light.svg" width="100%" align="top"></picture><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="./assets/page/stack-dark.svg"><img alt="Stack.
